key_insight: The paper proposes decomposing multi-agent LLM optimization into temporal credit assignment for critical rounds and structural credit assignment for agent roles to make sparse, discrete feedback tractable.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical, interpretable way to reduce query cost and stabilize self-improvement in LLM-based multi-agent systems by updating only the weakest components.
method: Use state-space bottlenecks to identify temporally critical interaction rounds.
Use stationary role policies to separate and score individual agent contributions.
Apply verbalized block coordinate descent to alternate between optimizing role prompts and aggregation protocols with LLM-generated proxy gradients.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated across diverse reasoning benchmarks, where the abstract reports lower query complexity and improved performance.
watch_item: Because it relies on LLM-generated proxy gradients and discrete coordinate updates, performance may be sensitive to prompt quality and optimization stability.
paper_title: Unifying Temporal and Structural Credit Assignment in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Prompt Optimization
